sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: What is the most important action for your eyes when preparing to catch a high-speed ball?
options: A) Look at your teammates for help
B) Keep them tracked continuously on the ball until it hits your hands
C) Close them right before impact to protect your face
D) Look at the ground to check your footing
questions.answer: B) Keep them tracked continuously on the ball until it hits your hands

questions.question_text: Which part of the foot should you primarily use to strike the ball for maximum power when kicking?
options: A) The very tip of the toe
B) The outside edge of the shoe
C) The hard instep (top of the foot where the laces are)
D) The bottom sole of the foot
questions.answer: C) The hard instep (top of the foot where the laces are)

questions.question_text: When throwing a ball over a long distance, what should your non-throwing arm do?
options: A) Hang loosely by your side
B) Point directly toward your target to help with aim and balance
C) Hold your waist to prevent twisting
D) Wave in the air to distract the opponent
questions.answer: B) Point directly toward your target to help with aim and balance

questions.question_text: Why do athletes use 'little steps' when approaching a moving ball or an opponent?
options: A) To slow down smoothly, maintain balance, and prepare to change direction
B) Because it looks stylish for the audience
C) To make louder sounds on the field
D) To jump higher into the air
questions.answer: A) To slow down smoothly, maintain balance, and prepare to change direction

questions.question_text: What does the term 'follow-through' mean when striking a ball with a bat?
options: A) Dropping the bat immediately after hitting the ball
B) Continuing the natural swing of the bat after it makes contact with the ball
C) Running after the ball once it is hit
D) Swinging the bat backward before hitting
questions.answer: B) Continuing the natural swing of the bat after it makes contact with the ball

questions.question_text: In a tactical game, how should you position your body to successfully intercept an opponent's pass?
options: A) Stand perfectly still and wait for the ball
B) Anticipate the path of the ball and step aggressively into the passing lane
C) Turn your back and hide behind a teammate
D) Run toward your own goal line
questions.answer: B) Anticipate the path of the ball and step aggressively into the passing lane

questions.question_text: When receiving a fast pass with your foot, what is the best way to keep the ball close to you?
options: A) Kick it back immediately as hard as you can
B) Stand with stiff, rigid legs to block it
C) Present the inside of your foot and slightly pull it back on contact to cushion the ball
D) Jump over the ball and trap it with your heels
questions.answer: C) Present the inside of your foot and slightly pull it back on contact to cushion the ball

questions.question_text: What is the correct stance before striking a moving object with a racket or bat?
options: A) Standing with feet completely together facing the target
B) Standing sideways to the target with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent
C) Sitting down to get a lower angle
D) Standing on one leg for better flexibility
questions.answer: B) Standing sideways to the target with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent

questions.question_text: What is the primary benefit of shifting your body weight from your back foot to your front foot while throwing?
options: A) It prevents you from falling backward
B) It generates more momentum, making the throw faster and more powerful
C) It allows you to see the target more clearly
D) It keeps your shoes from slipping on the grass
questions.answer: B) It generates more momentum, making the throw faster and more powerful

questions.question_text: If a ball is approaching your chest level rapidly, how should your fingers be positioned to catch it?
options: A) Pointing downwards toward the ground
B) Pointing directly at the ball
C) Pointing upwards with thumbs close together forming a 'W' shape
D) Closed into tight fists until the ball arrives
questions.answer: C) Pointing upwards with thumbs close together forming a 'W' shape

questions.question_text: Explain why the 'follow-through' motion is critical after throwing a ball toward a target. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The follow-through is critical because it ensures maximum throwing power, maintains balance, and directs the ball accurately toward the intended target without straining the arm muscles.

questions.question_text: Describe how to properly cushion and receive a fast-moving soccer pass with your foot. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: To cushion a fast pass, present the inside of your foot and slightly pull it back right as the ball makes contact, absorbing its speed to keep it close.

questions.question_text: What is the correct ready stance before striking an object with a bat or racket? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Stand sideways to the target with feet shoulder-width apart, bend your knees slightly, keep your eyes focused on the ball, and hold the bat firmly with both hands.

questions.question_text: How do 'little steps' help a player when preparing to stop or change direction quickly? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Taking little steps lowers your center of gravity and allows you to slow down smoothly, making it much easier to balance and push off in a new direction.

questions.question_text: Why is it important to move your body directly behind a ball when attempting to catch it? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Getting your body behind the ball provides a second barrier of defense. If the ball slips through your hands, your chest or torso can still stop it from passing.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are playing a team sport and need to intercept an opponent's pass. Describe the visual and physical steps you take to steal the ball successfully. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: I would closely watch the opponent's eyes and body language to predict the pass direction. As soon as the ball leaves their hands, I would use quick, explosive steps to sprint forward, reaching out with both hands to grab the ball mid-air before the receiver.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are about to strike a tennis ball with a racket. Describe how you position your feet and swing the racket for a powerful hit. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: I would quickly shuffle my feet to stand sideways to the net, planting my back foot firmly. I would pull the racket back, keep my eyes completely focused on the approaching ball, and swing forward smoothly, following through over my opposite shoulder.

questions.question_text: Explain the complete physical mechanics of taking a powerful and accurate penalty kick in soccer, from the run-up to the follow-through. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Start with a brief, angled run-up to build momentum. Plant your non-kicking foot firmly beside the ball, pointing your toes at the target. Swing your kicking leg back and strike the center of the ball with the hard instep of your foot. Finally, follow through powerfully in the direction of the goal to maximize speed and accuracy.

questions.question_text: Describe a tactical movement drill using 'little steps' and cones that helps improve a player's agility and ability to dodge defenders on the field. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Set up a zig-zag line of cones. Sprint toward the first cone, taking quick, little steps to brake and lower your hips as you approach it. Immediately plant your outside foot and pivot sharply to explode toward the next cone. This drill trains the fast deceleration and explosive acceleration needed to effectively dodge real defenders.
